# Panel J2, round 2: first-time visitor

I judged only from the panel sheets (1440 and 1024), `clips-panel.json` at both widths and the static scene sheets in `scenes/1440/`. The full per-screen list is in `panel-j2.json`.

## Scores (0 to 10)

| | Score |
|---|---|
| Keep scrolling | **7.5** (1440: 40/49 = 81.6% yes; 1024: 44/54 = 81.5% yes) |
| Tempo | **6.5** |
| Discovery | **5** |

## Yes rate and tempo by part

| Part (as I saw it) | 1440 yes | 1024 yes | Tempo | How it feels |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Opening: play screen, broom flight, name | 1/1 (100%) | 1/1 (100%) | brisk | A confident hook: Hogwarts, then a broom, then a glowing sea, then the name. |
| The Crossing (Pirates: porthole, contents, about, journey) | 6/7 (86%) | 5/7 (71%) | medium | Readable, steady scrollytelling. It runs out of steam on its last screen and drops into black. |
| The Workshop (3 Idiots: lecture hall to kill-list) | 9/15 (60%) | 11/18 (61%) | slow | It opens brilliantly, then three identical project cards, a skills table and a long kill-list drag for over a minute. This is where I would bail. |
| Three films and a game (four postcards) | 7/7 (100%) | 7/7 (100%) | brisk | Four worlds in about 30 s, each with a new palette. The best-paced stretch. |
| The Frontier (Red Dead: grey-to-gold, satchel, WANTED, journal, testimonials) | 10/12 (83%) | 12/13 (92%) | medium | Lots of material variety; only two text-heavy stops. |
| The Light (Great Hall, Marauder's Map, contact) | 5/5 (100%) | 5/5 (100%) | medium | It opens with a big hold on the Great Hall, then the map, where the walking footprints keep it alive. |
| Credits and "Mischief managed" | 2/2 (100%) | 3/3 (100%) | slow | A deliberate film roll and a satisfying close. |

## Where I said no

- **1440:** screen 8 (end of the journey, then black); 14 (a stats column); 16, 17 (the same project card again); 20, 21 (skills table); 23 (kill-list rows); 32 (the third identical act card, then black); 35 (text columns beside the horse).
- **1024:** screen 5 (an extra screen of About text); 8 (end of the journey, then black); 15 (stats); 17, 18, 19 (the repeated card, a blueprint colliding with the photo, more stats); 23 (skills); 25, 26 (kill-list rows); 38 (text columns).

The no's cluster in **The Workshop**. Everything else holds me.

## What invited me to play

| Thing | First seen | Would I try it? |
|---|---|---|
| Play button on the opening screen | 1440 s1 | yes. It is small, though, on a nearly empty screen. |
| "Director's cut (sound on)" | s1 | yes |
| Spyglass brackets around the ship and a compass on the hero | s1 | yes, I would hover them |
| Top-bar counter that looks like a hunt score ("… 0/12") | s1 | maybe. Unreadable while scrolling, so I would probably never notice it. |
| Contents list "A research journal in four acts" | s3 | maybe |
| Route-map nodes in the journey | s5 | maybe |
| "See the thesis, not just read it" chart (naive vs realistic) | s18 | yes |
| Small pill button on the drone photo (reads like "take off") | s19 | yes, if spotted |
| "Three films and a game" paragraph that seems to mention a game | s24 | maybe. Too small to read in passing. |
| Floating golden orb in the dark gap between the HP and Red Dead postcards | s30 (1024 s33) | yes. It is the strongest "click me". |
| X targets on the Red Dead sunset ("Dead Eye") | s28 | maybe. Clear on the still, nearly invisible while scrolling. |
| Satchel inventory icons with ticks | s36 | yes |
| WANTED poster with his name and a reply link | s36 (1024 s40) | yes |
| A fox running along the bottom of the journal | s38 (1024 s42) | yes |
| Marauder's Map footprints | s44 | maybe |
| Contact email, mail app, GitHub | s47 | yes |

The invitations are charming but almost all are **small and late**. The one thing that seems to explain "there is a game here" (the top-bar counter and the films-intro paragraph) is the hardest to read. On a steady scroll I would find the orb, the poster and the fox by luck, not because the page told me to look.

## In one line

A gorgeous, genuinely cinematic page that holds me about 80% of the way. The **Workshop** middle is the one place I would skim or leave, the **films** run is the high point, and the game is hidden too quietly for a casual scroller to find on purpose.
